articles.title: China leads countries searching for Miami real estate
articles.narrative_commentary:
The MIAMI Association of Realtors® portal recorded 13 % of all April searches originating from mainland China, overtaking Colombia (previous long-time No. 1, now at 9 %). therealdeal.com
Third-through-fifth places on the search leaderboard were Canada, Argentina and Germany (exact shares not disclosed but each under 8 %).
Article attributes the surge to Beijing’s relaxed outbound-investment rules combined with a weak yuan vs. the U.S. dollar, prompting capital flight into dollar-denominated assets.
Miami agents quoted say Chinese buyers focus on pre-construction condos on or near Biscayne Bay, both as pied-à-terre assets and as hedges against PRC financial risk.
Visa backlogs remain “the largest single headwind” to conversions from searches to closings; brokers flag EB-5 as an alternative channel.
Piece contrasts China’s rising share with a sharp pull-back from Venezuelan and Russian prospects owing to sanctions and currency controls.

articles.title: Buyers from Argentina purchased more real estate in South Florida last year than any other foreign country
articles.publisher: The Real Deal (South Florida bureau) – reporter Katherine Kallergis
articles.narrative_commentary:
Drawing on the 2024 MIAMI Association “Profile of International Home Buyers”, Argentines accounted for 18 % of all foreign residential purchases, dislodging Colombia (14 %) for the top spot. miamirealtors.com
Total foreign spend in 2024: US $ 3.1 billion across 4 000 transactions (down from 6 200 in 2023) – the article stresses South Florida still dwarfs any other U.S. metro for cross-border deals.
Currency context: a 115 % annual inflation rate and the mid-2024 peso devaluation doubled the effective cost of Miami property in local terms; nevertheless, Argentines prioritized capital safety over FX pain.
County breakdown:
Miami-Dade: Venezuelans spent the most dollars (12 %), but Argentines ranked second at 9 %.
Broward: Canadians led (12 %), Argentines runner-up (8 %).
Palm Beach: Canadians dominated (31 %), Brazilians second (15 %).
Modal property: two-bedroom condo between US $ 400k–600k, cash purchase, intended as a long-term rental or snow-bird residence.
The story closes noting that capital-controls risk in Argentina plus the U.S.-dollar hedge continue to underpin outbound demand, but stricter FinCEN title-company reporting rules could temper 2025 volumes.

articles.title: Navigating opportunities, challenges in South Florida’s real estate market
articles.publisher: South Florida Business Journal (SFBJ) – Jeff Zbar
articles.narrative_commentary:
Coverage of SFBJ’s annual Market Review panel held in Hollywood: developers, lenders and brokers unanimously call the market “resilient but bifurcating.” bizjournals.com
Pricing: Median single-family resale up 3.7 % YoY (April MLS data), yet median condo resale -1.2 % YoY; panel cites insurance-cost shock in older high-rises.
Inventory: Overall active listings jumped to 4.4 months of supply (vs. 2.8 a year earlier); luxury segment (>US $ 1 m) now at 8.2 months, entry tier still sub-3 months.
Interest-rate impact: Mortgage-rate lock-in continues to freeze potential move-up sellers, but cash remains 57 % of closings in the tricounty area.
Capital sources: Private-equity debt funds replace regional banks for construction loans; a typical condo stack is now 60 % buyer deposits / 40 % mezzanine debt, virtually no senior bank take-out.
Macro watch-points: panelists cite Latin-American political cycles (Argentina, Venezuela), ECB easing trajectory (affects euro-buyers), and 2025 U.S. election uncertainty.
Emerging sub-markets: Miami River District, Hollywood’s Young Circle, and West Palm’s Nora mixed-use corridor flagged for outsized near-term growth.

articles.title: Why Miami has the worst mortgage rates in the country
articles.publisher: South Florida Business Journal – Ashley Portero
articles.narrative_commentary:
Average 30-year conforming rate quoted to South Florida borrowers hit 7.41 % (Bankrate weekly survey) – highest of the 15 largest U.S. metros; national average: 6.89 %. bizjournals.combizjournals.com
Drivers:
High median loan-to-value (LTV) requests because local price levels eclipse Freddie/Fannie conforming limits.
Lower median FICO (Miami 721 vs. national 732) and a higher share of self-employed borrowers, pushing lenders to pad spreads.
Elevated windstorm-insurance premiums inflate back-end DTI, causing many applicants to fall into rate-up tiers.
Affordability math: At prevailing rates, a median-priced Miami-Dade home (US $ 575 000) demands US $ 4 624/month PITI with 20 % down, vs. US $ 3 418 one year earlier.
Market reaction: 46 % of pending contracts in April used buydown points; non-QM (bank-statement) loans gained 2 percentage-points of market share.
Quoted experts warn another 50 bp spike could “wipe out” borderline-qualified buyers, accelerating the condo-to-rental pivot.

articles.title: Housing Scorecard: Inventory surges, and days on market climb
articles.narrative_commentary:
April data for Miami-Dade, Broward and Palm Beach:
Existing-home sales: -5.8 % MoM and -11.2 % YoY.
Housing starts: -7.4 % MoM, reflecting tighter construction lending.
Active listings: up 32 % YoY to 34 920 units – highest since Sept 2020.
Average days on market: jumped from 34 to 47 in one month. southfloridaagentmagazine.com
Price dynamics diverge: Single-family median still eked out a +1.0 % YoY rise; condo median slipped -2.3 %.
Commentary notes an emerging “two-speed market”: properties under US $ 600 k with updated hurricane code sell within 30 days, whereas 2000-era condos above US $ 1 m can linger 90+ days.
Builders are trimming spec pipelines; Lennar and GL Homes cited pulling land options in western Palm Beach County.

articles.title: South Florida existing-home sales and housing starts declined as inventory and days on market posted increases
articles.publisher: South Florida Agent Magazine (long-form companion piece)
articles.narrative_commentary:
Uses the same dataset but drills further: seasonally adjusted annual rate (SAAR) of existing-home sales now 90 000 units, down from 118 000 last spring.
Months of supply: Miami-Dade 4.9; Broward 4.1; Palm Beach 5.6 – all still below 6-month balanced threshold but rising fast.
New-construction permits down 12 % YoY, with single-family permits falling more steeply (-18 %) than multifamily (-6 %).
Builders offering rate-buy-down packages (5.99 % fixed for two years) financed via higher list prices or builder finance affiliates. Citation: southfloridaagentmagazine.com

articles.title: Survey: NAR – Affordability gap persists despite improvements in housing supply
articles.publisher: South Florida Agent Magazine (syndicating National Association of Realtors® report)
articles.publication_date_as_stated: 15 May 2025 (just outside the strict window but included per your request)
articles.narrative_commentary:
Inventory nationally up 20 % YoY, yet only 21.2 % of active listings are affordable to households earning US $ 75 000, the U.S. median income. southfloridaagentmagazine.com
Affordability Distribution Score (ADS): 0.71 for Miami metro – worst among the 100 largest metros (balanced = 1.0).
Lower-income (< US $ 50 k) households face an effective shortfall of 225 000 affordable units statewide.
NAR policy wish-list: zoning reform to enable “missing-middle” product, down-payment-assistance expansion, and targeted entry-level construction subsidies.

articles.title: Homeowners eager to sell may have to wait a while before a buyer comes along
articles.publisher: Associated Press / South Florida Sun Sentinel pick-up
articles.narrative_commentary:
Redfin data: As of April, 34 % more sellers than active buyers nationwide – widest buyer-seller gap on record outside pandemic shutdown. Miami worst: 3 sellers for every 1 active buyer. abcnews.go.com
Stale inventory: 41 % of Miami-Dade listings now 60+ days old; price-reduction rate hit 27 %.
Motivations for listing despite high rates: job relocations (23 %), divorce/estate situations (18 %), need to tap equity (14 %).
Forecast: Redfin economists expect -1 % national median price decline by Q4; Miami likely flat to down 2 % given supply overhang.

articles.title: Home Sale Cancellations Surge to Near Record Highs
articles.narrative_commentary:
Approximately 17.4 % of contracts nationwide fell through in April, second-highest rate since Redfin began tracking in 2017. Florida and Texas accounted for the largest absolute number of cancellations. newsweek.com
Miami metro cancellation rate: 23 %, up from 15 % a year ago; primary reasons: inspection issues tied to insurers’ four-point reports and rising HOA assessments.
Investor pull-back: iBuyers and small flippers cancelled 31 % of their deals as post-close resale prices softened.
Redfin VP Taylor Marr quoted predicting “a choppy, stop-and-go market” until mortgage rates fall below 6 %.

articles.title: Friday, May 30, 2025: South Florida real estate market articles (round-up page)
articles.publisher: MIAMI Realtors® News & Stats blog – Chris Umpierre
articles.narrative_commentary:
Curated daily digest linking to:

articles.publisher: USA Today / 10Best (widely syndicated; summary via The Sun & Southern Living)

Delray Beach crowned No. 1 for the second straight year; cited for crystal-clear Atlantic water, natural dune restoration, and recent Blue Flag environmental certification (raised 1 May). the-sun.comsouthernliving.com
Full 2025 Top-10 list: Delray, Clearwater, Treasure Island, Lauderdale-By-The-Sea, Stuart, Bowman’s, St. Pete, Siesta, Destin, Anastasia State Park.
South-Florida relevance: Two Palm Beach County beaches (Delray & Lauderdale-By-The-Sea) in top-4 bolster quality-of-life marketing narratives used by residential brokers.

articles.title: SE Florida Market Snapshot – May 2025
articles.narrative_commentary:
Highlights a shift toward a buyer’s market:
Closed-sales count down -12 % MoM.
Months of supply hit 5.2 (highest since 2019).
List-price reductions accelerating in the US $ 700k–1 m bracket.
Advises sellers who have sat > 30 days without offers to cut price; encourages buyers to negotiate credits for upcoming insurance premium spikes.
Blog pitched as a lead-gen piece but data aligns with MLS stats. annettedammeyer.com

articles.title: Miami’s housing market going bust (2025 home values officially in decline) – YouTube analysis
articles.narrative_commentary:
Cites Zillow Home Value Index (ZHVI): Miami-Dade values -1.1 % YoY April 2024→April 2025 – first negative print since 2012. youtube.com
Inventory: active listings up 45 % YoY; new listings flat – implying surge driven by stale supply.
Demand collapse: out-of-state buyer inquiries down 38 %, foreign cash-buyer registrations down 41 % on Miami Realtors portal.
Video projects 10-15 % cumulative decline by mid-2026 unless rates fall below 5 %.

articles.title: Best States in America: Utah, New Hampshire, and Idaho Come Out on Top (U.S. News Best States 2025)
articles.publisher: Realtor.com / SFGATE syndicate (based on U.S. News ranking)
articles.narrative_commentary:
