This timeframe indicates a market that is moving at a steady, but not frenzied, pace. Overall, this quick snapshot portrays a Broward County single-family market that is functioning at a stable and moderate pace as of late October. The solid number of weekly sales and the relatively strong pricing metrics, combined with a reasonable time on market, point to a market that has likely found a level of equilibrium after the volatility of recent years, suggesting normalization.

articles.title: Lower mortgage rates extend housing momentum into fall
articles.summary: A September dip in mortgage rates provided a boost to the housing market, keeping both buyers and sellers unseasonably active, while the number of buyer's markets nationwide more than doubled over the past year, with Miami prominent among them.
articles.key_findings:
A decrease in mortgage rates during September helped to sustain housing market momentum into the fall season unexpectedly.
Both buyers and sellers remained more active than is typical for this time of year, spurred by the temporary rate drop improving sentiment.
The number of major U.S. metro areas classified as buyer's markets has more than doubled in the past year, rising from six to 15.
Miami is specifically identified as one of the strongest buyer's markets in the nation, alongside cities like New Orleans and Austin, due to high inventory.
articles.narrative_commentary:
The housing market received an unexpected boost in September thanks to a timely dip in mortgage rates, which helped to extend buyer and seller activity into the fall season at an unseasonably strong pace. This positive momentum, spurred by improved affordability, provided a welcome lift to a market that had been grappling with the effects of high borrowing costs for much of the year, according to Zillow's recent market analysis.
The decline in mortgage rates during September appeared to act as a significant catalyst, encouraging both sides of the market participants. Buyers who had been hesitant due to affordability concerns were drawn back in by the lower rates observed temporarily. At the same time, some sellers who might have otherwise waited may have been prompted to list their homes to capitalize on this renewed buyer interest, keeping overall activity levels elevated.
While this rate-induced momentum provided a short-term boost nationally, the broader market landscape continues its shift towards favoring buyers in many areas. The report highlights a dramatic increase in the number of major metropolitan areas that are now considered buyer's markets based on inventory levels. Over the past year, this number has more than doubled, indicating a widespread rebalancing across the country after years of seller dominance.
Miami is prominently featured among the cities leading this significant market shift toward buyers. It is identified as one of the strongest buyer's markets in the entire country, alongside other Sunbelt cities like New Orleans, Austin, and Jacksonville. This designation is based on factors such as exceptionally high inventory levels and longer times on market, which give buyers considerable negotiating power locally.
In conclusion, the fall housing market is presenting a complex and mixed picture nationally. The temporary dip in mortgage rates demonstrated the market's sensitivity to financing costs and unleashed some pent-up demand successfully. However, the underlying trend across many major markets, particularly in the South like Miami, is a continued movement toward conditions that are increasingly advantageous for buyers compared to recent years.

articles.title: Mortgage Rates Decrease to Lowest Level in Over a Year
articles.summary: The average 30-year fixed-rate mortgage dropped to 6.19%, its lowest level in over a year, spurred by Federal Reserve policy shifts and leading to a surge in refinancing activity which now accounts for over half of all mortgage applications.
articles.key_findings:
The average rate for a 30-year fixed-rate mortgage fell to 6.19%, marking its lowest level in more than 12 months.
Mortgage rates have now fallen nearly a full percentage point from their peak of over 7% seen earlier in 2025.
The lower rate environment has caused refinancing activity to surge significantly in recent weeks.
Refinancing applications have accounted for more than half of all mortgage applications for six consecutive weeks, the highest share in years.
articles.narrative_commentary:
In a continuation of positive news for the housing market, mortgage interest rates have decreased once again, reaching their lowest level in over a year. According to the latest weekly survey from Freddie Mac, the average rate on the benchmark 30-year fixed-rate mortgage has fallen further, providing additional relief to prospective homebuyers and existing homeowners looking to refinance their current loans at better terms.
The average 30-year rate now stands at 6.19%, a level not seen since October of the previous year. This marks a significant milestone, as rates have now fallen nearly a full percentage point from the peaks exceeding 7% that were observed earlier in 2025. This sustained downward trend is a crucial development for improving housing affordability across the board for potential buyers.
This lower rate environment is having a particularly dramatic impact on the refinancing market, which had been largely dormant. With rates now significantly lower than they were a year or two ago, a large wave of homeowners are rushing to refinance their existing mortgages. This is evidenced by the fact that refinancing activity has accounted for over half of all mortgage applications for six straight weeks.
This surge in refinancing is a clear indicator of the high degree of rate sensitivity among consumers. It demonstrates that homeowners are closely monitoring the rate environment and are poised to act quickly when conditions become favorable. This activity can also provide a boost to the broader economy, as lower monthly mortgage payments free up household income for other spending or saving purposes.
Overall, the continued decline in mortgage rates to a one-year low is a powerful and positive catalyst for the housing market. It is not only stimulating refinancing activity but is also contributing to the recent uptick seen in home purchase applications and closed sales. If this trend holds, it could pave the way for a more robust housing market recovery heading into 2026.

articles.title: Homebuyers Benefitting From A Sluggish Market
articles.summary: Housing market competition dropped to a six-year low in September, with the typical U.S. home selling for 1.4% below list price, clearly indicating buyers are benefitting from the current sluggish conditions and gaining negotiating power.
articles.key_findings:
Housing market competition nationwide reached its lowest level in six years during September, according to data from Redfin.
Only 25.3% of U.S. homes sold for more than their list price during the month, a significant drop from previous years.
The average sale-to-list price ratio fell below 100% to 98.6%, meaning the typical home sold for 1.4% below its final asking price.
In the South region, existing-home sales increased by 1.6% month-over-month, while the median price rose 1.2% year-over-year, showing some regional resilience.
articles.narrative_commentary:
The current U.S. housing market is offering significant advantages to homebuyers as competition has fallen to its lowest level in six years, creating decidedly sluggish conditions. Data from September clearly shows an environment where buyers have gained considerable negotiating power, and the days of widespread bidding wars and homes selling far above asking price appear to be largely over, providing welcome relief to purchasers navigating the market.
According to analysis from the real estate brokerage Redfin, a key indicator of market competition—the percentage of homes selling above list price—plummeted significantly in September. Only about a quarter of all homes sold for more than their asking price, a dramatic decrease from the peak frenzy of recent years. This clearly signals a major shift in the balance of power between buyers and sellers nationwide currently.
Further evidence of this crucial shift is the average sale-to-list price ratio, which fell below the 100% mark to 98.6%. This means that the typical home across the country is now selling for a discount—specifically, 1.4% below its final asking price on average. This is a significant development, confirming buyers are successfully negotiating prices down from listed amounts in most transactions happening today.
While the national picture shows a clear cooling trend overall, there are important regional variations to note. Data from the National Association of Realtors (NAR) indicates that the South region actually saw a slight month-over-month increase in existing-home sales in September. Additionally, the median price in the South posted a modest year-over-year gain, suggesting some pockets of resilience within the broader sluggish national trend.
Overall, however, the dominant national narrative is one of a market that is clearly favoring buyers after years of imbalance. The combination of low competition levels and the prevalence of homes selling below list price creates a much more advantageous environment for purchasers than has been seen recently. This presents a window of opportunity for those able to navigate affordability challenges successfully.

articles.title: China and Singapore lead web searches for South Florida real estate
articles.summary: Web searches from China and Singapore topped global interest in Miami real estate in September, signaling a potential new wave of Asian investment driven by policy factors like a paused foreign buyer law and a proposed U.S. investment visa.
articles.key_findings:
China and Singapore were the top two countries searching online for South Florida real estate in September 2025, displacing traditional leaders.
Colombia, typically a top source of searches, ranked third for the month, indicating a shift in global interest patterns.
The increased search volume from China may be linked to a temporary halt in the enforcement of Florida Senate Bill 264, which restricts purchases by certain foreign nationals.
Interest from Singapore could be driven by a proposed U.S. "Gold Card" program offering residency for a $1 million investment, below Singapore's own threshold.
articles.narrative_commentary:
A significant shift appears to be underway in the patterns of international interest in Miami real estate, with data from September 2025 showing a remarkable surge in online searches originating from Asia. For the first time, China and Singapore have claimed the top two spots globally for web searches targeting the South Florida property market, potentially signaling a new wave of investment from this influential region, adding diversity to the buyer pool.
This surge in Asian interest pushed Colombia, which has long dominated the search rankings for Miami property, down to the number three position for the month. This notable change suggests a broadening of Miami's global appeal beyond its traditional Latin American base. This shift could be driven by a confluence of specific policy factors and changing global economic conditions making Miami attractive.
Local experts suggest several potential catalysts for this increased attention from these specific Asian nations currently. The rise in searches from China might be linked to the temporary suspension of enforcement of Florida's controversial Senate Bill 264. This law aimed to restrict property purchases by citizens of certain foreign countries, including China; the pause may have reopened the door for some Chinese buyers.
Interest from the major financial hub of Singapore could potentially be related to a proposed new U.S. "Gold Card" program. This program would reportedly grant U.S. residency for a $1 million investment, a threshold significantly lower than Singapore's own investment visa requirements. This could make the U.S., and particularly attractive markets like Miami, a compelling destination for Singaporean investors seeking residency.
In conclusion, while Latin American buyers remain a dominant force in actual property purchases currently, the shift in online search patterns towards Asia is a significant development worth monitoring closely. It suggests that Miami's reach as a global investment destination is expanding, potentially opening up new and important sources of capital for the region's real estate market in the coming years and diversifying buyer origins.

articles.title: October 2025 Palm Beach County Real Estate Market Update
articles.summary: The Palm Beach County condo and townhome market presents a unique buying opportunity in October and November with stable prices ($310K median) and rising sales volume, allowing buyers negotiation leverage before seasonal competition potentially increases in January.
articles.key_findings:
The Palm Beach County condo market offers a strategic buying window in October and November before the busier winter season potentially increases competition.
Despite negative media narratives suggesting a crash, the median sold price for condos has remained relatively stable at $310,000 recently.
Sales volume for condos is actually up year-over-year, indicating healthy buyer demand is present in the market currently.
Buyers currently hold negotiating leverage, with properties selling at approximately 5-6% below original list price, but inventory trends show supply tightening slightly.
articles.narrative_commentary:
A market update focused specifically on the Palm Beach County condominium and townhome sector argues that the current fall season presents a unique and potentially advantageous window of opportunity for prospective buyers. The analysis suggests that despite some negative headlines about the broader market, the local condo segment is showing signs of stability and renewed activity, creating favorable conditions for purchasers right now before winter arrives.
Countering narratives of a market "freefall," the report highlights that the median sold price for a condo in the county has remained relatively stable at $310,000 recently. Furthermore, the total number of condo sales has actually increased compared to the previous year in recent reporting periods. These data points suggest that buyer demand is present and that the market is functioning in a healthy, albeit more balanced, manner.
The current environment is described as being favorable for buyers in terms of negotiation potential currently. Properties are selling, on average, for approximately 5-6% below their original list price, indicating that sellers are willing to be flexible to make a deal happen. Additionally, the moderate pace of the market allows buyers sufficient time for careful due diligence without the intense pressure of bidding wars.
However, the report cautions that this buyer-friendly window may be closing as the season progresses. While overall inventory levels have increased over the past 12 months, the recent trend line for available supply is now moving slightly downward as some sellers have withdrawn their listings from the market. This suggests that the inventory glut may be starting to ease somewhat locally.
The core message is one of strategic timing for potential condo purchasers in Palm Beach County. The analysis strongly advises buyers to consider acting during the October and November timeframe. Seasonal trends typically bring increased competition and potentially less seller flexibility during the peak winter buying season (January through March). Acting now allows buyers to capitalize on the current market balance.

articles.title: Miami Fall Real Estate Trends: What Buyers and Sellers Should Know in October 2025
articles.summary: Miami's fall real estate market is balanced but bifurcated, with high demand for luxury single-family homes (especially $10M+) contrasting with a slower mid-tier condo market facing affordability pressures from rising HOA fees and insurance, requiring strategic pricing from sellers.
articles.key_findings:
Miami's luxury market has steadied into a more balanced state, creating increased negotiating power for buyers compared to previous peak years.
The market performance is bifurcated: demand for luxury single-family homes, particularly those priced above $10 million, remains consistently high.
In contrast, the mid-tier condo market is experiencing longer selling times due to affordability challenges exacerbated by rising HOA fees and insurance costs.
Sellers in the current environment must be highly strategic with pricing to attract discerning buyers, as increased inventory allows purchasers to be more selective.
articles.narrative_commentary:
As the Miami real estate market moves into the fall season of 2025, the landscape is best described as balanced but highly segmented across different property types and price points. The extreme frenzy of the post-pandemic boom has clearly subsided, giving way to a more normalized environment overall. This significant shift has created increased negotiating power for buyers, while requiring sellers to adopt more strategic approaches, particularly regarding pricing.
The market is exhibiting a clear bifurcation in performance between these different segments currently. Demand for luxury single-family homes, especially those properties priced above the $10 million mark, remains remarkably high and resilient compared to other categories. This top tier continues to attract affluent buyers who are less sensitive to interest rates and are drawn by Miami's global appeal and unique lifestyle offerings, strongly supporting values.
In stark contrast, the mid-tier condominium market is facing more significant headwinds and slower activity overall. This segment is experiencing notably longer selling times and greater price sensitivity among potential buyers. A key factor contributing to this slowdown is the rapid escalation of carrying costs associated with condo ownership, particularly rising HOA fees driven by soaring insurance costs and new reserve requirements impacting affordability.
The fundamental driver of the market continues to be the influx of high-net-worth buyers relocating from high-tax states domestically and from various locations abroad. However, even this powerful demand source is operating within a new market context. With significantly more inventory available compared to the peak years, these affluent buyers can now afford to be more selective and patient, putting greater pressure on sellers.
In conclusion, navigating the Miami fall real estate market requires a nuanced understanding of these divergent performance trends effectively. While the luxury single-family sector remains robust, sellers in the mid-tier condo market must be particularly attuned to the challenges of overall affordability and rising carrying costs. For buyers, the increased inventory offers more opportunities, but careful consideration of long-term costs is crucial.

articles.title: Fisher Island, el código postal más caro de EEUU en 2025 (Fisher Island, the most expensive ZIP code in the USA in 2025)
articles.summary: Miami Beach's Fisher Island (33109) became the most expensive ZIP code in the U.S. with a $9.5 million median sale price after a 65% annual surge, marking the first time a Florida location has topped the list and highlighting the region's ultra-luxury boom.
articles.key_findings:
Fisher Island in Miami Beach has been named the most expensive ZIP code in the United States, with a median sale price of $9.5 million.
This was driven by a spectacular 65% year-over-year increase in its median price, dethroning Atherton, California after eight years.
It is the first time in history that the nation's priciest ZIP code is located in Florida, not California or New York.
The island's ultra-exclusivity is reflected in its sales range, with the highest sale reaching $23.7 million and the lowest still exceeding $1 million.
articles.narrative_commentary:
In a landmark achievement reflecting the intense concentration of wealth in South Florida, the exclusive enclave of Fisher Island in Miami Beach has been officially crowned the most expensive ZIP code in the entire United States for 2025. This prestigious title was secured after a period of extraordinary price appreciation that propelled its median sale price to unprecedented levels, surpassing all other locations nationally.
Fisher Island's median sale price reached an astonishing $9.5 million, boosted by a massive 65% surge compared to the previous year. This meteoric rise was sufficient to dethrone the long-standing leader, Atherton, California (ZIP code 94027), which had held the top spot for nearly a decade. This marks a significant geographical shift in the pinnacle of American luxury real estate values.
This achievement holds historical significance for Florida. It represents the first time ever that the nation's most costly ZIP code is situated within the Sunshine State, breaking the traditional dominance of ultra-wealthy enclaves in California and New York. This underscores the dramatic transformation and consolidation of South Florida's market as a premier global destination for luxury property investment attracting immense capital.
The range of prices on Fisher Island highlights its extreme exclusivity and appeal to the world's elite. While the highest sale recorded during the year reached nearly $24 million, even the least expensive transaction still commanded a price tag exceeding $1 million. Accessible only by private ferry or yacht, the island offers unparalleled privacy and five-star amenities to its very small number of residents.
Fisher Island's ascent symbolizes the broader boom occurring in South Florida's ultra-luxury real estate sector. Fueled by a massive influx of wealth migration and international capital seeking stability and exclusivity, areas like Fisher Island have seen values skyrocket. This reflects Miami's solidified status as a global epicenter for luxury living and investment attracting discerning buyers worldwide.

articles.title: Calta Group proposes Anatomia apartments and condos in Miami using Live Local Act
articles.summary: Leveraging Florida's Live Local Act, Calta Group has proposed a 30-story tower in Miami's Health District combining 210 workforce housing units with 299 market-rate condos, showcasing the law's potential to spur mixed-income development.
articles.key_findings:
Calta Group plans a 30-story, 499-unit residential tower ("Anatomia") in Miami's Health District near major hospitals.
The project utilizes Florida's Live Local Act, setting aside 40% of units (about 210 apartments) as workforce housing for those earning up to 120% of AMI.
In exchange for the affordability component, the project can achieve greater height and density than typically allowed by local zoning.
This represents one of Miami's first major projects combining a large affordable/workforce component with market-rate condos in the same tower under the new state law.
articles.narrative_commentary:
A new development proposal in Miami's Health District showcases the potential of Florida's recent "Live Local Act" to facilitate the creation of mixed-income housing projects. Calta Group has unveiled plans for a substantial 30-story residential tower, named "Anatomia," which aims to combine market-rate condominiums with a significant number of workforce housing units, made possible by the state's pro-housing legislation designed to boost supply.
The project is planned for a one-acre site near the University of Miami/Jackson Memorial hospital complex and envisions a total of 499 residential units. Crucially, leveraging the Live Local Act, the developers intend to designate 40% of these units—approximately 210 apartments—as workforce housing. These units would be reserved for households earning up to 120% of the area median income (AMI), addressing the critical need for housing for middle-income essential workers.
The Live Local Act incentivizes developers to include affordable components by allowing them to bypass certain local zoning restrictions, such as height and density limits. In this case, Calta Group can build a larger project than would otherwise be permitted, making the inclusion of the workforce housing financially feasible while still delivering 299 market-rate condominiums within the same structure, a novel approach locally.
This project represents one of the first major examples in Miami of a developer utilizing the Live Local Act to create a vertically integrated mixed-income building combining both rental apartments and for-sale condos. This innovative approach could serve as a model for future developments seeking to address the region's housing affordability crisis while still achieving market-rate returns necessary for project financing and viability.
The proposal is currently moving through the city's review process, with hopes to break ground by mid-2026 if approvals are secured. Its progress will be closely watched as a test case for how effectively the Live Local Act can spur the development of much-needed workforce housing within privately funded, market-rate projects in South Florida's urban core, potentially reshaping future development patterns significantly.

articles.title: ‘Quiet luxury’ is coming for the housing market, Corcoran Group CEO says. It’s not just the Hamptons, Aspen, and Miami anymore.
articles.summary: A trend of "quiet luxury" is redefining the high-end housing market, with affluent buyers prioritizing understated comfort, quality, and privacy over ostentatious displays, and seeking these smaller, high-design homes in emerging luxury markets beyond traditional hubs.
articles.key_findings:
Corcoran Group CEO Pamela Liebman identifies a shift towards "quiet luxury" in the high-end housing market.
Affluent buyers increasingly prefer understated homes focused on comfort, privacy, and quality craftsmanship over sheer size or opulence.
Data shows the average size of new U.S. homes has decreased, reflecting a move towards smaller, high-design properties, often purchased with cash.
The luxury boom is spreading beyond traditional enclaves like Miami and Aspen to emerging scenic, relaxed areas like Sonoma County and Park City.
articles.narrative_commentary:
The definition of luxury in the high-end housing market is undergoing a significant transformation, according to Pamela Liebman, CEO of the prestigious Corcoran Group brokerage. A new trend, dubbed "quiet luxury," is emerging where affluent buyers are increasingly prioritizing understated elegance, personal comfort, quality materials, and privacy over the ostentatious displays of wealth that may have characterized previous eras.
This shift represents a change in mindset among wealthy purchasers seeking different values. Exclusivity is becoming less about showcasing wealth through sheer size or grandeur and more about creating a personal sanctuary that enhances lifestyle. Features like intimate outdoor living spaces, bespoke artisan details, or sustainable design elements are now often valued more highly than massive foyers or sprawling high-maintenance estates reflecting this trend.
Data trends appear to support this shift towards a more refined, less excessive form of luxury living currently. The average size of newly built homes in the U.S. has actually decreased in recent years, suggesting that even at the high end, buyers are opting for quality over just quantity. Many affluent buyers prefer these smaller homes with top-tier finishes, easier to manage and often purchased with cash.
This trend is also contributing to a geographic diversification of the luxury market across the United States currently. While traditional hotspots like the Hamptons, Aspen, and Miami remain highly desirable locations, wealthy buyers seeking this "quiet luxury" lifestyle are increasingly flocking to emerging markets. Scenic, relaxed areas offering natural beauty and high quality of life are seeing surges in high-end activity from discerning purchasers.
In essence, "quiet luxury" reflects a move toward a more personalized and experience-driven definition of high-end living for today's buyer. It's less about the property as a conspicuous status symbol and more about the home as a private haven that brings personal joy without necessarily drawing widespread external attention. This evolving preference is reshaping demand patterns and development priorities within the luxury sector.
This evolving preference focuses on homes feeling like sanctuaries for their owners rather than just investments. The upshot is a potentially more personalized and resilient luxury market segment that is less tied exclusively to trophy mansions and more focused on subjective quality of life attributes valued by the individual buyer seeking comfort and privacy in their residence.

articles.title: Miami-Dade Ultra-Luxury Sales on Pace to Set Records; Affordable 30-Year Condo Units Holding Value
articles.summary: Miami-Dade's real estate market is highly bifurcated, with sales of homes over $10 million on pace for a near-record year, while at the other end, older and more affordable 30-year-old condo units are also holding their value well, demonstrating strength at both extremes.
articles.key_findings:
South Florida is on track to have its second-best year ever for home sales priced at $10 million and above.
In the first seven months of 2025, Miami-Dade saw a 115% year-over-year increase in single-family home sales priced above $3,000 per square foot.
The median price for older, 30-year-old condo units held its value well, with a median price of $294,000, supporting entry-level affordability.
The overall condo market faces headwinds, with a high 14.1-month supply of inventory indicating a strong buyer's market, contrasting with the balanced single-family segment.
articles.narrative_commentary:
The real estate market in Miami-Dade County is demonstrating a profound and dramatic bifurcation, with exceptional strength at the very top and surprising resilience at the most affordable end of the spectrum. This "barbell" effect shows two very different market realities playing out simultaneously, with the ultra-luxury and entry-level segments both outperforming the middle of the market which faces more typical cooling trends observed nationally.
At the highest end, the ultra-luxury market is having a banner year despite broader economic shifts. South Florida is currently on pace to record its second-highest number of home sales over $10 million in a single calendar year, nearly matching pandemic-era records. The data for Miami-Dade is particularly stunning, with the number of single-family homes selling for over $3,000 per square foot having more than doubled year-over-year, showcasing intense demand.
At the opposite end of the market spectrum, the more affordable segment of older condominiums is also holding its value remarkably well. The median price for condo units in buildings that are 30 years or older has remained stable, with only a very slight dip from the previous year. This price resilience in the entry-level tier is a crucial element supporting relative affordability for local buyers and first-time purchasers.
These two areas of strength stand in contrast to the broader market's performance, particularly within the general condo segment. The overall median prices for both single-family homes and condos in the county saw slight year-over-year declines in July. The condominium market, specifically, is heavily tilted in favor of buyers, with a massive 14.1-month supply of available inventory creating significant pricing pressure for mid-range units.
A key factor contributing to the oversupply and challenges in the broader condo market is the ongoing difficulty with financing options. An extremely low percentage of condo buildings in the region are approved for FHA loans, which severely limits the pool of potential first-time and financed buyers for these properties. This structural issue remains a major headwind for the health of the non-luxury segment of the condominium market.
Furthermore, the strength observed at both ends is bolstered by consistent demand drivers. The report reiterates that international buyers account for nearly half of new construction sales, underscoring the powerful global demand that supports Miami's market. This international capital, often deployed as cash, helps insulate parts of the market from domestic interest rate fluctuations, contributing to the observed bifurcation in performance across price points.

articles.title: Broward County $1M & Up Condo Sales Rise
articles.summary: Despite a drop in total condo sales and median prices, Broward County's luxury condo market showed exceptional strength in July, with sales of units over $1 million surging by 79% year-over-year, accompanied by an increase in cash buyers.
articles.key_findings:
Sales of condominiums in Broward County priced at $1 million and above increased by a massive 79% year-over-year in July 2025 (from 24 to 43 sales).
This surge in the luxury tier occurred even as the total number of condo sales in the county fell by 7.5% overall.
The number of cash buyers for condos also increased by 8.6% year-over-year (from 524 to 569), signaling a strong presence of affluent, non-financed purchasers.
The median sale price for condos in the overall market was $265,000, which is down 2.75% from the previous year, highlighting the market split.
articles.narrative_commentary:
The condominium market in Broward County is exhibiting a stark and dramatic bifurcation, with the luxury segment showing incredible strength while the broader market continues to experience a cooldown phase. The latest data from July 2025 reveals that the demand for high-end, million-dollar-plus condos is not just resilient but is actually accelerating rapidly, a trend running counter to the general market's overall performance metrics.
The most striking statistic is the explosive 79% year-over-year surge in the number of sales for condos priced at $1 million and above. This massive increase demonstrates a powerful and sustained appetite from affluent buyers for premium properties within the county. This performance at the top end is a major bright spot in an otherwise moderating market environment for condominiums in Broward currently.
This luxury boom is occurring at the same time that the overall condo market is contracting noticeably. The total number of condo sales in the county actually fell by 7.5% year-over-year, and the median sale price saw a modest decline of 2.75%. This clear divergence vividly shows that the market is not moving in a single direction; the luxury tier is operating on a completely different, more robust track presently.
A key factor supporting the remarkable strength of the high-end market is the prevalence of cash buyers making purchases. The number of all-cash condo purchases in the county increased by 8.6% from the previous year. This indicates the strong presence of wealthy, non-financed buyers who are less sensitive to the high mortgage rates sidelining many purchasers in more mainstream segments of the housing market.
Meanwhile, the overall inventory of homes for sale in Broward has continued to grow, pushing conditions toward balance for single-family homes but firmly into buyer's territory for condos (12 months' supply). Financing remains a significant hurdle, especially for condos, with fewer than 1% of buildings FHA-approved regionally, limiting options for many potential first-time and financed buyers needing lower down payments.

articles.title: Palm Beach County Single-Family Home Sales Increase
articles.summary: In a notable divergence from the regional trend, single-family home sales in Palm Beach County rose by 1% year-over-year in July, showing unique resilience, though median prices for both houses (-4.85%) and condos (-6.1%) continued to decline modestly.
articles.key_findings:
Sales of single-family homes in Palm Beach County increased by 1% year-over-year to 1,185 transactions in July 2025.
This positive sales growth is a notable contrast to the significant declines that were seen in the neighboring counties of Miami-Dade and Broward during the same period.
The median sale price for single-family homes fell by 4.85% year-over-year to $613,250, indicating price adjustments are still occurring.
The inventory for condominiums has expanded to a 9.3-month supply, indicating a strong buyer's market for that specific property type within the county.
articles.narrative_commentary:
The Palm Beach County real estate market is showing a unique and resilient performance profile, particularly within its single-family home sector, which demonstrated positive sales growth in July. This is a significant development, as it runs counter to the trend of declining sales seen concurrently in the other major South Florida counties. This suggests that buyer demand in Palm Beach has remained particularly robust through the summer season compared to neighbors.
The key data point from the July report is the 1% year-over-year increase in the number of closed sales for single-family homes, reaching 1,185 transactions. While a modest gain numerically, the fact that sales are growing at all in the current high-interest-rate environment is a sign of the market's underlying strength and appeal. This performance notably sets Palm Beach apart from Miami-Dade and Broward counties currently.
However, this increase in sales activity has not prevented a market-wide price correction from continuing. The median sale price for a single-family home in the county actually decreased by nearly 5% compared to the previous year. Similarly, the median condo price fell over 6%. This shows that even in a market with relatively strong demand, sellers are still needing to adjust pricing expectations downward.
The inventory situation in the county reveals a clear split between the two main property types, mirroring regional trends. The supply of single-family homes has reached 5.5 months, approaching a balanced state but still leaning slightly in favor of sellers. The condominium market, conversely, has seen its inventory expand significantly to a 9.3-month supply, which firmly establishes it as a buyer's market locally.
A persistent structural challenge impacting the condo market in Palm Beach, mirroring the entire region, is the severe lack of financing options available for buyers. The extremely small number of condo buildings that are approved for FHA loans severely restricts the pool of potential first-time and financed buyers needing lower down payments. This remains a major headwind contributing to condo oversupply currently.

articles.title: South Florida residential sales volume drops 10% in July
articles.summary: The total dollar volume of residential sales across South Florida fell by 10% to $4.5 billion in July, with median prices declining year-over-year in all three counties for both single-family homes and condos, marking a broad regional cooldown.
articles.key_findings:
The total dollar volume of residential sales in the tri-county area decreased by 10% year-over-year to $4.5 billion in July 2025.
For the first time in the current cycle, median prices fell year-over-year for both property types (single-family homes and condos) in all three counties simultaneously.
Miami-Dade saw the largest drop in the number of sales transactions, which fell by 16% year-over-year.
Total sales volume also fell in Broward (-7%) and Palm Beach (-5%), confirming a consistent region-wide slowdown in market activity during July.
articles.narrative_commentary:
The residential real estate market across South Florida experienced a broad-based and significant slowdown in July, with all three major counties recording year-over-year declines in sales volume and, notably, median prices across the board. This synchronized downturn marks a new phase in the region's market correction, indicating that the cooling trend is now affecting all parts of the tri-county area in a consistent and measurable manner, impacting overall value transacted.
The most encompassing measure of this clear cooldown is the 10% year-over-year drop in the total dollar volume of all residential sales combined, which fell to $4.5 billion for the month across the region. This decline in the total amount of money being spent on real estate is a strong sign of a market with both fewer transactions occurring and moderating prices, reflecting a clear pullback in overall activity levels.
A particularly significant development observed in the July data was that, for the first time in the current market cycle, median prices declined year-over-year for both single-family homes and condominiums in all three counties simultaneously. This across-the-board price drop confirms that the price correction, previously more segmented, is now a universal regional phenomenon affecting all major property types and locations within South Florida.
The decline in the actual number of transactions was also a consistent theme across the region, though the severity varied somewhat by county. Miami-Dade experienced the steepest drop in the number of closed sales compared to the previous year. The sales volume also decreased notably in both Broward and Palm Beach, confirming that market headwinds like high rates are impacting buyer demand everywhere.
In conclusion, the July sales data provides a clear and cohesive picture of a regional market that is now fully entrenched in a corrective phase. The synchronized declines in dollar volume, sales counts, and median prices across all three counties and both major property types leave little doubt that the post-pandemic boom has definitively ended and a new, more challenging market cycle has firmly taken hold across South Florida.
